audit.whatIsWrong: diff says FAV but difficulty reads 8.5/10 and the rating line says 'Hard matchup'.
audit.why: 56.29% over 1917 games is the second-best win rate in this slice. The lane is genuinely hard for three levels and then decisively Olaf's — 'hard overall' is the wrong headline.
audit.corrected: diffRating to 6/10 with breakdown.difficulty and report[14] matched; the early pain is kept in the phase text where it belongs.

audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 4, 5 and 6 gave the late stages to Jayce while the whys under them say the opposite.
audit.why: whys[4] says level 6 flips to you, whys[5] calls first item unbeatable, whys[6] says you still beat him in melee — and the packet chart reads Olaf for all three.
audit.corrected: Rows 4, 5 and 6 flipped as one atomic group in both layers, ratings 7/6/6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three strings say Ragnarok 'cleanses' or 'strips' Thundering Blow's knockback and his slows.
audit.why: Ragnarok is passive resists plus immunity to disables while he keeps attacking. It removes nothing already applied, and Riot's text does not establish that a knockback or a slow is covered — so the honest line is the immunity itself, held by continuing to swing.
audit.corrected: Rewritten in whys[4], spikes[1], mid and wants.you[0]; no displacement-immunity claim made.

audit.whatIsWrong: Six strings give Olaf's W omnivamp or sustain.
audit.why: Tough It Out is attack speed plus a shield on 16s at rank 1; the lifesteal is the passive and scales with MISSING health — against a poke laner that is the whole point, because the poke he lands makes your healing stronger.
audit.corrected: Split correctly across tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, whys[3], whys[5], spikes[2], late and wants.you[2].

audit.whatIsWrong: The packet flags it directly: no cooldown sequencing anywhere in the entry.
audit.why: Shock Blast is 16s at rank 1 falling to 6s; Thundering Blow is 20s falling to 10s; Undertow is a flat 9s that refunds on pickup and Reckless Swing 11s. Those are the numbers a walk-up decision actually turns on.
audit.corrected: Shock Blast's 16s and Undertow's 9s written into breakdown.early, tradeGood and phases[0].why.

edits.before: Overall difficulty: 8.5/10. The lane is decided by how well you track Shock Blast and how disciplined your pattern is.
edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you survive Shock Blast to 6 and how hard you punish after.

edits.before: Hard matchup — difficulty 8.5/10, Jayce carry threat 8/10.
edits.after: Favourable matchup — difficulty 6/10, Jayce carry threat 8/10.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Identify how Jayce contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Shock Blast through the Acceleration Gate out-ranges everything you own — soak XP and don't contest the first waves.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Respect Jayce's Shock Blast completely — the first levels are about banking small advantages, not proving a point.
edits.after: Undertow's slow and Tough It Out's shield are all you have early. Respect Shock Blast — 16s at rank 1 — because these levels are about surviving, not proving a point.

edits.before: Land the axe slow on Jayce, walk the pickup for the reset, reave the true damage, and W-sustain whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields his answer.

edits.before: Land the axe slow on Jayce, walk the pickup for the reset, reave the true damage, and W-sustain whatever he answers with.
edits.after: Undertow him as he steps up, walk the pickup to reset its 9s, then Reckless Swing — Tough It Out shields his answer.

edits.before: Your W omnivamp and axe-reset slows let you survive and stick — the lane levels out as you close the gap.
edits.after: Your missing-health lifesteal and axe-reset slows let you survive and stick — the lane levels as you close.

edits.before: Ragnarok cleanses his knockback and slow, so you walk through the poke and all-in him with E true damage he can't kite.
edits.after: Ragnarok keeps you disable-immune while you keep swinging, so his poke can't peel and Reckless Swing finishes it.

edits.before: Your Black Cleaver / Bramble plus W omnivamp makes the sustained all-in unbeatable — chain Q-slows and he can't escape.
edits.after: Black Cleaver / Bramble plus missing-health lifesteal makes the all-in unbeatable — chain axe slows and he can't escape.

edits.before: Ragnarok cleanses his E knockback and his cannon slows, so you walk through the poke and force the melee all-in he cannot answer.
edits.after: Ragnarok holds his disables off while you keep swinging, so you walk through the poke and force the melee all-in he cannot answer.

edits.before: Black Cleaver / Bramble plus your W omnivamp makes your sustained all-in oppressive — chain Q-slows and he can't kite out.
edits.after: Black Cleaver / Bramble plus missing-health lifesteal makes your all-in oppressive — chain axe slows and he can't kite out.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 even out as your W omnivamp and axe-reset slows let you survive his poke and start sticking to him. Then Level 6 flips the lane hard: Ragnarok strips his E knockback and cannon slow off you, so you charge through the poke unstoppable and force the melee all-in. Land Q to perma-slow, E his face for true damage, and let your passive attack speed ramp as you take his poke. He has no answer once you're on top of him.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 even out as your missing-health lifesteal and axe-reset slows let you survive his poke and start sticking to him. Then Level 6 flips the lane hard: Ragnarok keeps you disable-immune as long as you keep attacking, so Thundering Blow stops peeling and you force the melee all-in. Undertow to perma-slow, Reckless Swing to his face, and your attack speed ramps as his poke lands. He has no answer once you're on top of him.

edits.before: Your first-item bruiser spike (Black Cleaver, Bramble, W omnivamp) is your most oppressive point — every all-in heals you up and his burst can't trade with your sustain. But past two items Jayce reclaims the matchup: his range and full burst combo chunk you before you commit, and your flat true damage stops scaling. Convert your early-to-mid lead into towers, dives, and objectives — don't let this go to a poke war at three items.
edits.after: Your first-item bruiser spike (Black Cleaver, Bramble, missing-health lifesteal) is your most oppressive point — every all-in heals you up and his burst can't trade with that. But past two items Jayce reclaims the matchup: his range and full burst combo chunk you before you commit, and your flat true damage stops scaling. Convert the early-to-mid lead into towers, dives and objectives — never a poke war at three items.

edits.before: Hit Level 6 and use Ragnarok to ignore his E knockback and cannon slow on the all-in
edits.after: Hit 6 and keep swinging under Ragnarok so his disables never land on the all-in

edits.before: Use W omnivamp to heal through his poke and end the lane before two items
edits.after: Let the missing-health passive heal his poke back, and end the lane by two items

notes: The page carried a 56.29% win rate and an 8.5/10 'Hard matchup' label at the same time, with the level chart giving Jayce levels 6, first item AND two items while the whys under those rows all said Olaf. Rows 4-6 flipped and the difficulty brought to 6/10; if the user prefers the old number, the diffRating, breakdown.difficulty and report[14] edits revert together.
